title: Gas Station
description: Brute force to optimized: simulating the full circuit from every starting station versus a single pass with a greedy reset rule.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: There are n gas stations along a circular route, gas[i] being the gas available at station i, and cost[i] being the gas needed to travel from station i to station i+1. Starting with an empty tank at some station, return the index of the starting station that allows completing the entire circuit (going around once), or -1 if no such starting station exists (the answer is guaranteed unique if one exists).

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["\"Circular route, find a valid starting point\"","Track a running tank; whenever it goes negative, no station up to and including the current one could be a valid start"],["Feasibility overall depends on total gas versus total cost","A single global sum check first determines whether ANY solution exists at all"]]}

blocks.text: If the total gas available across all stations is less than the total cost to travel the whole circuit, no starting point can work, since the overall deficit is unavoidable. Otherwise, exactly one starting point works, and it can be found by tracking a running tank: whenever the tank goes negative starting from some candidate, that candidate (and every station up to the point of failure) cannot be the answer, so the search resumes from the very next station.

blocks.title: Analogy: Finding Where a Road Trip Can Begin Without Running Out of Fuel
blocks.text: Picture a circular road trip with fuel available and fuel needed varying at each stop, and wanting to know where to start so you never run out of fuel along the way. If your fuel tank ever goes negative starting from a candidate stop, that stop (and everywhere before the point of failure) cannot be the answer, so the only hope is to start from right after where you ran out.

blocks.caption: A negative running tank means the search must resume from right after the failure point

blocks.text: Result: 3. Starting from station 3, the tank never goes negative while completing the full circuit.

Before simulating the full circuit from every possible starting station, notice that if the running tank ever goes negative starting from some candidate station, EVERY station between that candidate and the point of failure also cannot be a valid start (since starting from any of them would run out even sooner or at the same point), so the search can jump directly past the failure point.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: If total gas is less than total cost, it is mathematically impossible to complete the circuit from ANY starting point, so the answer is immediately -1.

Observation 2: Otherwise, track a running "tank" value, starting a candidate journey from station 0; whenever the tank goes negative at some station i, no station from the current candidate start up through i could have been a valid starting point either, since they would all run out at or before this same point.

Observation 3: When the tank goes negative, reset the candidate start to i+1, and reset the tank to 0, continuing the scan from there.

Observation 4: Since the overall total gas is guaranteed sufficient (from Observation 1), the LAST candidate start found this way is guaranteed to be the unique valid answer.

This leads to a single pass: track a running tank and total; whenever the tank goes negative, reset the candidate start to the next station and the tank to 0. If the overall total is non-negative, the final candidate start is the answer; otherwise, -1.
Try starting from every possible station, simulating the full circuit from each and checking whether the tank ever goes negative.

items: For each candidate starting station, simulate traveling the full circuit, tracking the tank level.
If the tank never goes negative throughout the full circuit, this starting station is valid.
Return the first (and, per the problem's guarantee, only) valid starting station found, or -1 if none work.

codes.python:
def can_complete_circuit_brute(gas, cost):
    n = len(gas)
    for start in range(n):                              # try every starting station
        tank = 0
        valid = True
        for i in range(n):
            station = (start + i) % n
            tank += gas[station] - cost[station]
            if tank < 0:
                valid = False
                break
        if valid:
            return start
    return -1

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Simulating the full circuit from every starting station directly checks each candidate, guaranteed correct.
This costs O(n squared) in the worst case, unnecessary once the "jump past the failure point" insight is applied.

blocks.text: Limitation: since a failed candidate start also invalidates every station up to the failure point, a single pass can skip directly past them, achieving O(n) instead of O(n squared).

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why simulating from every station is unnecessary: if starting from station s, the tank goes negative at station f, then starting from ANY station between s and f (inclusive) would ALSO go negative at or before f, since they would begin with less or equal accumulated surplus at that point.

The single-pass reset rule: maintain a running tank across a single forward pass; whenever it goes negative, reset the candidate start to the very next station and reset the tank to 0, continuing the scan.

Checking overall feasibility: separately track the total gas minus total cost across the whole circuit; if this is negative, no starting point can ever work, regardless of the reset logic's result.

The core idea: one pass, resetting the candidate start whenever the tank goes negative, combined with a global feasibility check.

Track a running tank and a running total across a single pass. Whenever tank goes negative, reset the candidate start to the next station and tank to 0. After the pass, return the candidate start if total >= 0, otherwise -1.

blocks.caption: A single pass with a reset rule finds the valid starting station directly

codes.python:
def can_complete_circuit(gas, cost):
    total = 0
    tank = 0
    start = 0
    for i in range(len(gas)):
        diff = gas[i] - cost[i]
        total += diff
        tank += diff
        if tank < 0:                        # this candidate start (and everything before) fails
            start = i + 1
            tank = 0
    return start if total >= 0 else -1

blocks.text: If the tank goes negative while starting from candidate station s and reaching station f, every station between s and f (inclusive) also fails as a starting point, since starting later within this range only means LESS accumulated surplus by the time station f is reached, making failure even more certain. Resetting the candidate to f+1 correctly skips all these guaranteed-invalid options in one step. Since the problem guarantees a unique valid answer whenever total gas is sufficient, the last candidate start surviving the full pass is exactly that answer.

blocks.text: Gas Station is a classic greedy problem demonstrating that a failed candidate invalidates an entire RANGE of other candidates at once, letting a single pass skip directly past them instead of retrying each individually.

items: Forgetting the separate global total check, which is what confirms a solution exists at all (the reset logic alone finds A candidate, but only the total check confirms its validity).
Resetting only the start index without also resetting the tank to 0, corrupting subsequent calculations.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "circular route, find a feasible starting point", think: single pass, reset the candidate start whenever the running total goes negative.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: Simulating from every starting station costs O(n squared) time; the single-pass reset approach costs O(n) time, both using O(1) space.

items: Pattern: a single pass with a reset rule, since a failed candidate invalidates an entire contiguous range of other candidates at once.
Core Idea: track a running tank; reset the candidate start to the next station whenever the tank goes negative; the global total confirms a solution exists.
Time: O(n squared) for simulating every start, O(n) for the optimized single pass.
Most Important Observation: a failed starting candidate also invalidates every station up to the point of failure, letting the search skip directly past them.
Interview Difficulty: a classic, frequently asked greedy problem with an elegant single-pass solution.
One line memory trick: reset the candidate start whenever the running tank goes negative; check the global total for overall feasibility.
